title: End-to-End Latency-Minimizing and Load-Balanced Request Scheduling for Edge LLM Inference in Agentic AI Services
abstract: arXiv:2609.17193v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language model (LLM)-powered agentic AI services increasingly demand low-latency inference, motivating the deployment of LLMs across distributed edge servers. However, heterogeneous communication and computing capabilities, together with dynamically evolving inference states, make the edge server selection for each incoming request time-varying and tightly coupled across slots. In this paper, we investigate an online request scheduling framework for edge LLM inference that jointly minimizes long-term average end-to-end latency and regulates workload distribution across heterogeneous edge servers. Two main challenges arise in this context. First, conventional latency models cannot accurately capture the fine-grained dynamics of multi-stage LLM execution. translated_title: 面向智能体AI服务中边缘LLM推理的端到端延迟最小化与负载均衡请求调度
translated_abstract: arXiv:2609.17193v1 公告类型：新 摘要：由大语言模型（LLM）驱动的智能体AI服务日益需要低延迟推理，这促使LLM被部署于分布式边缘服务器之上。然而，异构的通信与计算能力，加上动态演变的推理状态，使得针对每个传入请求的边缘服务器选择具有时变性，且在各时隙之间紧密耦合。本文研究了一种用于边缘LLM推理的在线请求调度框架，该框架联合最小化长期平均端到端延迟，并调节异构边缘服务器之间的工作负载分布。在此背景下产生了两个主要挑战：其一，传统的延迟模型无法准确捕捉多阶段LLM执行的细粒度动态；其二，调度决策的延迟后果只有在请求完成后才能被观察到，使得即时决策评估变得困难。为应对这些挑战，我们……
tldr: 本文提出了一种面向边缘LLM推理的在线请求调度框架，通过联合最小化长期平均端到端延迟并均衡异构边缘服务器间的负载，解决了传统延迟模型无法刻画多阶段LLM执行动态以及调度后果滞后观察这两大难题。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes an online request scheduling framework for edge LLM inference that jointly minimizes long-term average end-to-end latency and balances workloads across heterogeneous edge servers, addressing the challenges of modeling fine-grained multi-stage LLM execution dynamics and the delayed observability of scheduling decisions.
